name: Imipramine
route_note: Oral tablets or capsules; IM formulation historically available.

discovery.note: Synthesised by Geigy in 1951 as a chlorpromazine-like antihistamine; Kuhn observed its antidepressant effect in 1956 and reported it in 1957.

tagline: The first tricyclic antidepressant, discovered by chance in a Swiss hospital
summary: Imipramine was the first tricyclic antidepressant. Its mood-elevating effect was discovered by psychiatrist Roland Kuhn in 1956 while testing a chlorpromazine analogue, and it helped launch the monoamine theory of depression. It is still used for depression and childhood nocturnal enuresis.
mechanism: Imipramine inhibits reuptake of serotonin and noradrenaline; its metabolite desipramine is a potent and selective noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor. It also blocks muscarinic, histamine H1 and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors.
The action in enuresis is thought to involve anticholinergic effects on the bladder and changes in sleep architecture and arousal.

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Geigy synthesises imipramine (G 22355) as an iminodibenzyl analogue of phenothiazines.

history.title: Antidepressant effect
history.detail: Roland Kuhn observes striking improvement in depressed patients at the Münsterlingen hospital.

history.title: Publication
history.detail: Kuhn reports his findings in the Schweizerische Medizinische Wochenschrift and at a congress in Zurich.

history.title: Launch
history.detail: Geigy markets imipramine as Tofranil in Switzerland.

history.title: United States
history.detail: Imipramine becomes available in the US.

history.title: Monoamine hypothesis
history.detail: Joseph Schildkraut's catecholamine hypothesis of depression builds on tricyclic and MAOI pharmacology.

safety.boxed_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours in children, adolescents and young adults (under 25) taking antidepressants; monitor for clinical worsening.

facts: Kuhn's discovery came from clinical observation in a few dozen patients rather than an animal model.
